title: The hypertrophy series: eccentric vs concentric movements
summary: Introduction to the negative (eccentric) and positive (concentric) phases: the negative stores energy released in the positive, you are strongest on negatives and weakest at the bottom, positive-only lifts like deadlifts express full strength but yield less tonnage, and most of a program should use full-range lifts with both phases: slow negative, fast positive.
claims: Every lift has a positive and negative phase, plus an isometric component in some, and the ratio changes the quality of tonnage
I prefer 'positive' and 'negative' to concentric and eccentric because programming is complicated enough
During the negative the muscle lengthens and stores energy, released in the positive like a spring
Partial-rep cheating nearly always cuts the bottom of the negative because you are weakest at the deepest point, where leverage is most compromised
Form breakdown usually happens at the reversal from negative to positive
Strength order: pure negative strongest, negative-then-positive middle, positive-only weakest because no stretch reflex
Hypertrophy value cannot be assigned universally by phase; it depends on the lift and range of motion
Most of your lifts should involve a negative; a majority of positive-only lifts is a mistake
In a squat the negative is sandbagged relative to the positive because you are stronger eccentrically
Positive-only lifts like the deadlift express 100% strength where you are mechanically weakest, so saying deadlifts do not build size is wrong
Do not slowly lower deadlifts: you do the strong phase in a fatigued state, risking structural damage; use RDLs with adjusted intensity instead
Lifts with both phases accumulate much more tonnage than positive-only lifts even if you can lift more positive-only
Some muscles respond well to positive-only partials, but most do not, so full range of motion is the default
My philosophy: full range of motion, slow negative for tension, fast positive
exercises: drop it rather than lowering slowly
to train the deadlift negative safely
